summary.headline: Websol FY26 revenue rose 82% to INR 1,049 crore and PAT 96% to INR 303 crore, with Q4 revenue of INR 401 crore and a INR 1,161 crore order book.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue of INR 1,049 crore (up ~82%), EBITDA of INR 429 crore (41% margin) and PAT of INR 303 crore (28.6% margin), with Q4 the best quarter on most parameters. The company turned net cash surplus, cash from operations was INR 255 crore, and cell capacity doubled to ~1.2 GW after cell line 2 commissioning in September 2025. Management plans to upgrade one 600 MW Mono PERC line to TOPCon (capacity to 1.35 GW) by February 2027, while Andhra Pradesh expansion timing remains undisclosed beyond a June 2027 target. Margin compression was attributed to a higher module mix, silver costs and softer cell and module realisations.

segments.name: Cells (DCR)
segments.commentary: Combined cell utilisation above 90% in FY26; cell realisation ~13-13.5 cents/Wp, softening with silver cost increases. Cells supplied to module makers and captive use in the company's own module line.

segments.name: Modules (DCR)
segments.commentary: Highest-ever module sales in Q4; module realisation ~22-22.5 cents/Wp. Module line (550 MW, Mono PERC) hit a record monthly utilisation of 80%. Module margins are structurally lower than cell margins and drove most of the EBITDA margin dip.

guidance_outlook: TOPCon upgrade of one 600 MW Mono PERC line to ~750 MW (+150 MW), commercial start targeted February 2027, ~2 months ramp to full utilisation; capex INR 250-270 crore; ~15 days revenue loss for that line.
Management expects to approach full run-rate utilisation across all lines in the coming quarter (Q1 FY27).
Andhra Pradesh expansion (2 GW integrated cell and module phase) targeted for June 2027 per management; details to be announced later, no postponement planned.
Ingot and wafer backward integration, with MOU signed with Linton, targeted to commission ahead of ALMM List-3 deadline of June 2028.
Cell and module margins expected to remain healthy over the next 2-3 years with some variability, per management.
capex_capacity: Cell capacity doubled from 600 MW to ~1.2 GW with cell line 2 commissioned in September 2025, funded entirely from internal accruals.
Mono PERC to TOPCon upgrade takes cell capacity to ~1.35 GW; target cell efficiency above 24.5% (vs ~23.3% for PERC); cell size moving from 182x182 to G12R (182x210).
Integrated 4 GW cell and module plan in phases of 2 GW each; the second 2 GW tranche expected around mid-CY28 on TOPCon, with space reserved for future back-contact upgrade.
Module capacity is 550 MW; cell capacity exceeds module capacity, so about 600-750 MW of cell output is sold to third-party module makers.
Management says there is little scope for further expansion at the existing Falta site.
demand_pricing: Focus is on DCR market, mainly PM-KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar; management reports no demand issues and says its entire line is ALMM-listed and DCR-compliant.
Order book is largely module (60%) and mostly sold through solar pump and module players; the company does not tender directly for government orders.
Current TOPCon DCR cell price ~14 cents/Wp; cell realisation 13-13.5 cents/Wp and module 22-22.5 cents/Wp, described as a softening.
Management says it is seeing more orders than the reported INR 1,161 crore but did not quantify further bookings.
Q4 off-take recovered after Q3 delays that were attributed to temporary customer liquidity stress rather than cancellations.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline to repay the IREDA loan and release pledged promoter shares?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt under the IREDA facility is ~INR 92 crore and more than 80% of promoter shares are pledged; advanced discussions are under way, with completion expected in the next month or two.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 EBITDA margin decline driven by?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop mainly to higher module share in the mix, plus silver cost increases and softer cell sale prices; EBITDA still grew 86% YoY and ~37% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TOPCon upgrade capex, revenue loss and ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is INR 250-270 crore for ~150 MW of added capacity; revenue loss is about 15 days for the one line, and ramp-up to full utilisation is ~2 months after February 2027 commercial start.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company move to lower depreciation lives and what is the FY27 tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: TOPCon equipment useful life is now 8 years (from 12 years) and Mono PERC is 3 years; all tax credits are used up, so FY27 will be at the standard corporate tax rate.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company fund the next capex phase?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus cash covers near-term expansion, with some debt to be raised later; management aims to keep debt levels prudent and said there is no funding concern for now.

qa_highlights.question: Does management see any update on the Andhra Pradesh timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is targeting June 2027, has not postponed the commitment, and will announce details once the funding structure and sequencing are finalised.

risks_watch: Silver cost increases and cell price softening are compressing margins; management says variability is expected over the short to medium term.
Execution risk on the Andhra Pradesh expansion (June 2027 target) and the 2 GW phase, with management not yet announcing a final sequencing or funding structure.
TOPCon upgrade in Feb 2027 includes roughly 2 months of ramp-up, and the 15-day line outage could affect near-term output.
Working capital rose, with higher inventory and receivables. Management says receivables are largely backed by letters of credit from prime banks.
Ingot and wafer integration (June 2028 ALMM-III target) is at MOU and team-building stage, with capex not yet confirmed and Linton commercial terms undisclosed.
Future debt raising for the expansion, given the company is currently net cash surplus.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and financial results, but deliberately vague on the next expansion: timelines, funding and Andhra Pradesh details were repeatedly deferred to later announcements. Management was defensive on margin and pricing outlook, calling the market dynamic and declining to quantify module versus cell margins.
key_quotes: We have delivered the highest revenue, the highest EBITDA and the highest PAT in the company's history.
Our balance sheet is the strongest it has been in our 30-year journey.
We are targeting cell efficiency of more than 24.5% on this upgraded line.
I think June 2027 is what we are targeting.

growth.why: No explicit FY27 revenue growth number is guided; management expects near full run-rate utilisation in Q1 FY27 and a TOPCon upgrade (+150 MW, INR 250-270 crore capex) by February 2027, backed by a INR 1,161 crore order book (book-to-bill 1.02x), while the Andhra Pradesh 2 GW expansion is targeted for June 2027 but its details remain undisclosed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 EBITDA margin fell from ~41% FY26 average pressure as module mix rose, silver cost increased and cell realisation softened to 13-13.5 cents/Wp; management called cell and module margins healthy over 2-3 years but with variability, so no expansion is guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (TOPCon upgrade commercial start by February 2027)
rows.why: Cell capacity is ~1.2 GW after line 2 in September 2025 with utilisation at 90%, and the approved Mono PERC to TOPCon upgrade adds 150 MW (600 to 750 MW line) to reach ~1.35 GW, capex INR 250-270 crore.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Cell utilisation is 90% and management expects near full run-rate across all lines in Q1 FY27, backed by a INR 1,161 crore order book (book-to-bill 1.02x) and ~INR 412 crore of new orders in the quarter, with +150 MW from February 2027.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 90% with only a 150 MW upgrade planned and little room at the Falta site, so the Andhra Pradesh 2 GW phase (targeted June 2027) and second 2 GW TOPCon tranche (around mid-CY28) need a formal announcement, though management has deferred sequencing and funding details.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects near full run-rate utilisation across all lines in Q1 FY27 and sees more orders than the INR 1,161 crore book, but gave no quantified FY27 revenue guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Silver cost increases and cell price softening (cell realisation 13-13.5 cents/Wp, module 22-22.5 cents/Wp) are compressing margins, and the 15-day revenue loss from the TOPCon upgrade plus the 2-month ramp could weigh on Q4 FY27 numbers.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: TOPCon cells at above 24.5% efficiency (vs ~23.3% PERC) and a move to G12R (182x210) are planned with the Feb 2027 commercial start of the upgraded line.

rows.label: IREDA loan repayment and promoter pledge release
rows.why: Net debt under the IREDA facility is ~INR 92 crore and more than 80% of promoter shares are pledged, with advanced discussions under way and completion expected in a month or two.

rows.label: Receivables and inventory build
rows.why: Working capital rose with higher inventory and receivables, though management says receivables are largely backed by letters of credit from prime banks, and Q3 off-take delays were attributed to customer liquidity stress.

rows.label: Ingot and wafer backward integration (Linton MOU)
rows.why: MOU signed with Linton with the ALMM List-3 deadline of June 2028 as target, but capex is unconfirmed and commercial terms are undisclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on operations and the 90% utilisation and order book, but deferred Andhra Pradesh timing, funding and sequencing and was defensive on margin and pricing outlook as silver costs and cell prices pressured margins.
